title: The Forged Will
briefing: A will was forged on Friday, by the nephew or by the family lawyer. You only have two rules to work with here, and they are not enough for a direct proof. Assume the opposite of what you want to show and look for a contradiction.

atoms.T: The nephew was in town on Friday
atoms.I: The will is written in blue ink

statements.speaker: Handwriting expert
statements.text: Only two people could copy that signature. The nephew forged it, or the lawyer did.

statements.speaker: Solicitor's clerk
statements.text: The will never left our office. If the nephew forged it, he was in town on Friday.

clues.text: His passport is stamped: he was abroad all week, so he was not in town on Friday.
The will is written in blue ink.

tip: With these two rules a direct proof is impossible. Press "Assume the opposite", then derive a formula and its negation.
